content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I occasionally encounter an issue where I'm unable to remove a connection terminal within the network view, which forces me to delete the entire project and start over. The terminal appears grayed out and does not respond to any delete commands (see attached screenshot). Deleting the whole project does not resolve the problem either. Can anyone explain why this happens? Program Version: [version_no] Program Timestamp: 2016-07-15 08-49 Language Used: en_US Language Version: [version_no] Updates: OS Name: Windows 7 OS Version: 6.1 Processor: amd64
Please upload your project. That will make it easier to assist you.
I've attached the project file. You may need to change its extension to .7z depending on which unzip tool you're using.

I'm unable to precisely follow the steps you took to create this connection. I managed to delete a connection from the right [product_name], but the other link on the left [product_name] couldn't be removed. I also noticed there isn't any entry in the connection list. Without additional details, I can't provide further recommendations.

The right [version_no] connection was created by me in an attempt to reproduce the undeletable issue. I'm not sure where the IP address for the left connection came from. That connection appeared on its own, possibly after uploading (device > PC) HW settings, diagram data, and modifying the program diagram. I've sent this issue to Support.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is facing a sporadic issue where certain network connections within the software's network view cannot be deleted, as the delete option becomes disabled. Attempts to delete the entire project do not resolve the problem, resulting in disrupted project workflows. The issue is tied to the software's interface and may necessitate project re-creation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the ability to delete any network connection or terminal freely while editing a project, and for the software to consistently execute user commands without errors.
